title: 用 PMA 看懂 Claude Code：一次工具调用

source.viewer_diff_since_capture: The capture commit is not an ancestor of origin/main, but the trees under src/viewer, src/server, and src/contracts/viewer-api.mjs are identical between the capture commit and origin/main.
source.real_cli_cross_check: The assistant/tool_use -> user/tool_result -> final response shape is separately present in the Claude Code 2.1.220 real-CLI Skill trace. This two-request teaching Source itself is synthetic and must not be described as a real provider session.

audiences: 第一次想知道 Claude Code 为什么能读取文件的用户
想区分远端模型决策与本地 Harness 执行的开发者
需要核对 Anthropic tool_use、tool_result、调用标识与消息角色的 Harness 工程师
teaching_contract.question: 远端模型只能输入和输出结构化文本，为什么 Claude Code 最终却能读取本地 README？
teaching_contract.takeaway: 模型从请求中声明的工具里返回 tool_use；Claude Code 负责权限检查与本地执行，再把同一调用标识的 tool_result 放入后续 user message；模型收到新请求后才形成最终回答。PMA 把模型参数、System、Tools、调用、结果、来源跳转、协议和 Raw 证据放进一条可导航链。
out_of_scope: 真实 provider 性能或模型质量评测
Claude Code 的内部思维链

scenario.task: 请读取 README.md 第一行，告诉我项目名；不要修改文件。
mechanism_flow: Request 1 声明 System 与 Tools

viewer.capture_method: Codex in-app Browser controlling the PMA Viewer
viewer.layout: full three-pane Viewer; no browser chrome, black frame, or baked annotation

facts: The teaching Source contains one PMA Turn and two Anthropic Messages requests.
Request 1 Metadata shows model, max_tokens, stream, transport identity, token usage, and upstream composition.
Request 1 System contains only fictional /demo constraints and explicitly forbids credentials, user files, and network access.
Request 1 declares Read, Glob, and Bash with descriptions and input schemas.
Request 1 response contains tool_use id read_hello for Read(README.md, offset=1, limit=1).
Request 2 contains a user-role tool_result with the same read_hello id and output '# hello-agent'.
The Viewer links the result back to its originating call and preserves a return-to-result action.
The Protocol view preserves the Anthropic role order: user, assistant text, assistant/tool_use, user/tool_result, and final assistant response.
The Raw Inspector displays the complete synthetic headers and body while showing sensitive headers as redacted.
The final response says '项目名是 hello-agent。' and can be traced backward to the tool result.

raw_frames.focus: Request 1 model and common request parameters

annotation_policy: A label tab that already names itself, such as System, Tools, Metadata, Protocol, Raw, or Response, uses a focus outline without a redundant numbered badge.
Numbered markers are reserved for actions and evidence that need a reading order; they appear one at a time in narration order.
Independent focus changes crossfade for approximately 0.7 seconds and remove the previous marker.
When source state and call details must remain visible together, the earlier outline remains but uses dim_ms to become secondary when the new numbered evidence appears.
No routed arrow is used because focus outlines, pane position, click pulse, and source state already establish every relationship.
The final Details action uses one short click pulse instead of a numbered marker near the subtitle safe area.

notes: The full three-pane Viewer remains visible and no browser or video black frame surrounds it.

The first v0.2 draft placed Metadata, tool_result, and Response focus boxes one tab too far right. All three coordinates were corrected and the affected crossfade states were re-recorded at both sizes.

A second review found that numbered badges on already-labelled tabs covered the right-pane title. Those badges were removed; tabs now use a light focus outline and numbering begins on the evidence itself.
Badge numerals remain visually centered at both review sizes.
The source-navigation scene retains a dimmed source-state outline when the call parameters appear, preserving causality without two equally strong numbered markers.
The final-response click pulse was reviewed against the actual Details button center.
The old recording/review and video/frames directories are v0.1 comparison artifacts and are not v0.2 publication sources.
